site.description: wunder is an agent orchestration platform: Honeycomb (desktop) is the local AI workbench, Beehive (web) is the cloud AI workbench, Helm (cli) is the manual local entry point, and the Hull (server) is the user and agent management platform. / wunder 是一个智能体调度平台：蜂窝（desktop）是本地 AI 工作台，蜂巢（web）是云端 AI 工作台，舵机（cli）是手工本地操作入口，舰体（server）是用户与智能体管理平台。

pages.title: wunder 心舰
pages.summary: wunder 是智能体调度平台。蜂窝是电脑上的本地 AI 工作台，蜂巢是浏览器里的云端工作台，舵机是终端入口，舰体是多人共用的管理平台。

pages.title: 快速开始
pages.summary: 用最短路径把蜂窝跑起来：下载、启动、配模型、发第一条消息、验证结果。个人用户默认入口，无需部署服务。

pages.title: 蜂窝（desktop）入门
pages.summary: wunder 的默认使用方式：本地 AI 工作台。下载安装即可使用，不需要先部署舰体；同进程原生调用引擎，不占端口，不走 HTTP/WebSocket 中转。

pages.title: 舰体（server）部署
pages.summary: 可选形态。多人共用的用户与智能体管理平台：多租户、权限治理、渠道接入、智能体应用发布。舰体启动后同端口挂舰桥（18000），蜂巢由独立的网页服务容器下发（18001）。

pages.title: 舵机（cli）使用
pages.summary: 手工本地操作入口。终端里进交互界面，管道里自动降级为一次性执行；22 条斜杠命令、exec --json 事件流、cloud 子命令全套；舵机侧关闭定时任务与引擎排队。

pages.title: 说明书总览
pages.summary: 说明书导航页：从蜂窝起步，按需进入界面地图、其它形态与参考。start 与 surfaces 两组的全部页面都在这里。

pages.title: 常用说明目录
pages.summary: 仓库文档生态导航：设计文档、技术说明书、API 文档、使用说明书、性能标准与评分、功能迭代、经验教训的分工与读法。

pages.title: 核心概览
pages.summary: wunder 为什么这样表现——10 个核心设计约束，以及它们的分层与入口。

pages.title: 智能体循环
pages.summary: 你只说一次目标，剩下的步骤引擎替你跑：循环按模型轮次推进，到终态或刹车为止。

pages.title: 工具
pages.summary: 智能体做事的能力来自四层结构——执行体工具、可调用知识与脚本的技能、管理员选择的能力、用户自己接入的工具；四层不是一回事，「能选」不等于「能调」。

pages.title: 上下文压缩
pages.summary: 长对话不会因为太长而中断：系统在必要时精简历史、保留最有效的信息，让对话继续。

pages.title: 记忆
pages.summary: 长期资料在线程创建时注入一次，之后保持冻结。它的两层结构，以及使用上的注意点。

pages.title: 渠道
pages.summary: 飞书、QQ、微信、XMPP 和通用 webhook 各自的支持范围，以及消息到智能体与工作区的绑定解析。

pages.title: 定时任务
pages.summary: 智能体在指定时间自动执行：at 定点、every 固定间隔、cron 表达式三种排程，配租约、退避与自动禁用，进程重启不丢任务。

pages.title: 多用户管理
pages.summary: 舰体形态下的用户、单位与权限边界：登录态、在线状态、单位树、等级与额度、智能体定义文档和数据隔离。

pages.title: 实时性

pages.title: wunder
pages.summary: wunder is an agent orchestration platform. The Honeycomb is the local AI workbench on your computer, the Beehive is the cloud workbench in a browser, the Helm is the terminal entry point, and the Hull is the shared management platform for teams.

pages.title: Quick Start
pages.summary: The shortest path to get the Honeycomb running: download, launch, configure a model, send your first message, verify the result. The default entry point for individual users, with no service to deploy.

pages.title: Starting with the Honeycomb (Desktop)
pages.summary: wunder's default way to work: a local AI workbench. Download, install, open, go — no Hull to deploy first; it calls the engine natively in-process, takes no port, and routes through no HTTP/WebSocket relay.

pages.title: Deploying the Hull (Server)
pages.summary: An optional form. The user-and-agent management platform for multi-user sharing: multi-tenancy, permission governance, channel integration, and agent-app publishing. Once the Hull is up, the Bridge (18000) is served on the same port, and the Beehive is delivered by a separate web-service container (18001).

pages.title: Using the Helm (CLI)
pages.summary: The manual local entry point. In a terminal it opens an interactive session; in a pipeline it degrades to a one-shot run. The full set of 22 slash commands, an exec --json event stream, and the complete cloud subcommand family; scheduled tasks and engine queueing are off on the Helm.

pages.title: Manual Overview
pages.summary: The manual's navigation page: start from the Honeycomb and move into the interface map, other forms, and reference as needed. Every page in the start and surfaces groups is here.

pages.title: Documentation Directory
pages.summary: A guide to the repo's documentation ecosystem: how the overview and design docs, technical manual, API reference, user manual, performance standards and scoring, changelog, and lessons-learned divide the work, and how to read them.

pages.title: Core Concepts
pages.summary: Why wunder behaves the way it does—10 core design constraints, along with the layers they form, the entries into them, and the reading paths.

pages.title: Agent Loop
pages.summary: You state the goal once and the engine runs the remaining steps; the loop advances round by round until it reaches a deliverable result or hits a brake.

pages.title: Tools
pages.summary: The agent's ability to act comes from a four-layer structure: executor tools, skills that package callable knowledge and scripts, capabilities the administrator selects, and tools the user connects. Keeping the layers distinct is what keeps "selectable" separate from "invokable".

pages.title: Context Compression
pages.summary: Long conversations are not cut short when they grow long. The system trims history in graded levels, keeps the most useful information, and lets the conversation continue.

pages.title: Memory
pages.summary: Long-term data is injected once when a thread is created and stays frozen afterwards; it has two layers, initialization injection and runtime recall.

pages.title: Channels
pages.summary: Feishu, QQ, WeChat, XMPP, and generic webhooks differ in support level; an inbound message is routed to its agent and workspace by binding.

pages.title: Scheduled Tasks
pages.summary: Scheduled tasks run the agent at a chosen time: three schedule kinds — at for a one-off point, every for a fixed interval, cron for a recurring pattern — with leases, backoff, and auto-disable, so tasks survive a process restart.

pages.title: Multi-user Management
pages.summary: User, unit, and permission boundaries in the Hull form: login state, presence, the unit tree, levels and quotas, agent definition documents, and data isolation.

pages.title: Realtime
pages.summary: The realtime channel runs on WebSocket; a reconnect catches up by cursor; what the client sees is a projection of backend truth; slow clients are uncoupled to protect the stream.

pages.title: Stability
pages.summary: Errors that do not spread, failures that can recover, and problems that can be reviewed. Stability comes from four kinds of hard constraint — bounds, budgets, circuit breaking, and a single writer — plus a consistent error structure and clear actions when something goes wrong.

pages.title: Observability
pages.summary: Logs, runtime metrics and alerts, monitoring and thread traces, and performance testing each cover their own area; failures are worked through in a fixed order from the error message onward.

pages.title: Tools Overview
pages.summary: wunder's tools are grouped by purpose: selection entry points by situation, the conventions for how results are shaped, and a few exceptions.

pages.title: Workspace Files
pages.summary: Browsing the workspace, searching content, reading files, and writing files.

pages.title: Execute Command
pages.summary: Run shell commands, compile, test, or call an existing command-line tool; it supports previews, resource budgets, and output guards.

pages.title: ptc
pages.summary: ptc was the temporary Python script execution tool; it has been removed from wunder, and this page is a historical reference.

pages.title: Apply Patch
pages.summary: Use patch text for small, reviewable, precise edits; `apply_patch` has been merged into `Text Edit`.

pages.title: Read Image
pages.summary: Send a local image, animated GIF, or video into the current conversation so the agent can look at the material directly.

pages.title: Skill Call
pages.summary: Loading a skill's instructions and its directory into the current conversation so the agent can work through that skill's process.

pages.title: Web Fetch
pages.summary: Letting the agent read the body of a web page, for looking things up, reading docs, or inspecting API responses.

pages.title: Browser Tools
pages.summary: The browser is not a single tool: once enabled it registers a group of `browser_*` tools for opening pages, clicking, typing, waiting, taking screenshots, and reading rendered content.

pages.title: Desktop Control
pages.summary: In desktop mode, the Desktop Controller and Desktop Monitor drive the local mouse and keyboard, capture screenshots, and feed the picture to the model as appended visual input.

pages.title: Plan Panel / Question Panel / Sessions Yield
pages.summary: Three interaction-control tools: maintaining a visible execution plan, asking the user for a route before acting, and yielding the current turn to wait for an external event.

pages.title: Schedule Task
pages.summary: Creates, changes, inspects, runs right away, and enables or disables scheduled jobs.

pages.title: Final Response
pages.summary: The Final Response tool has been removed from wunder; kept only as a historical reference.

pages.title: Sessions Yield
pages.summary: Letting the agent stop the current turn on purpose, hand control back to the system, and carry on once an external result arrives.

pages.title: Thread Control
pages.summary: Letting the agent move several things forward at once: create, switch, rename, archive, and restore task threads.

pages.title: Subagent Control
pages.summary: Letting the main agent hand a self-contained piece of work to subagents, then track, wait on, guide, and reclaim them.

pages.title: Memory Manager
pages.summary: Manage the current agent's long-term memory fragments under the current user: list, search, read, add, update, and remove, along with the "short index injection plus fetch-on-demand" pattern.

pages.title: Channel Tool
pages.summary: The channel tool has been removed from wunder; kept only as a historical reference.

pages.title: Self Status
pages.summary: Checks the current session's model, context usage, round progress, and event counts, for deciding whether to compress context or wrap up.

pages.title: User World
pages.summary: Looking up which users exist inside the site, and sending messages to users inside the site.

pages.title: A2A Tools
pages.summary: A2A tools have been removed from wunder; kept only as a historical reference.

pages.title: Integration Overview
pages.summary: Each integration need has its own entry: one-off execution, chat sessions, workspace, temporary conversion, external channels, passwordless embedding, A2A, and MCP.

pages.title: wunder API
pages.summary: Call wunder as an execution capability — one request, one result; move to the chat domain when you want a full chat product.

pages.title: Chat WebSocket
pages.summary: The real-time channel for chat and also the session control channel: starting an execution, resuming after a disconnect, watching, canceling, and returning approvals all happen on the same connection.

pages.title: Chat Sessions
pages.summary: The session interfaces for building a chat product: creating sessions, sending and receiving messages, attachment preprocessing, resuming, and canceling all live in this domain.

pages.title: Workspace API
pages.summary: The workspace does more than file read and write — it pins every user to their own single cloud directory.

pages.title: Temp Directory and Document Conversion
pages.summary: Temporary uploads, downloads, and transit all go through the temp directory; documents, audio, and video get one conversion or media pass before they enter a session.

pages.title: User World API
pages.summary: One-to-one chats, group chats, and read state between users all live here, parallel to the user-to-agent conversation domain.

pages.title: Channel Webhook
pages.summary: Inbound messages from external channels (Feishu, WeChat, QQ, XMPP, and others) all arrive through a single Webhook address and are then handled asynchronously in the background.

pages.title: WeChat iLink Channel
pages.summary: The new WeChat channel uses the iLink protocol and is not the same thing as the legacy Official Account or WeCom channels.

pages.title: External Login and Embedding
pages.summary: Bring users who are already logged in to an external system straight into wunder without asking them to type a password again; they can land on the chat page or on a specific agent.

pages.title: A2A Interface
pages.summary: wunder both exposes its capabilities to other agent systems over the A2A protocol and mounts external A2A services as tools the model can call.

pages.title: MCP Endpoint
pages.summary: wunder can both expose itself as an MCP service and act as an MCP client to connect to external services.

pages.title: Interface Overview
pages.summary: Four forms, four interfaces — the Honeycomb (local AI workbench), the Beehive (cloud AI workbench), the Helm (terminal interface), and the Bridge (admin governance console). Look up interface capabilities by form.

pages.title: Beehive Interface
pages.summary: The Beehive is the cloud AI workbench, provided with the Hull deployment and reached in a browser. Its settings include tools, memory, channels, scheduled tasks, devices, and archive; it supports two-way voice (TTS included) and has no interactive terminal.

pages.title: Bridge Interface
pages.summary: The Bridge is the Hull's governance and debugging console. Its top-level navigation has 4 groups and 19 items: System 4, Agents 6, Debug 6, Docs 2.

pages.title: Honeycomb Interface
pages.summary: The Honeycomb (desktop) is the local AI workbench and the default entry for individual users. Its main window has only two pages, chat and settings, with 12 categories in settings; everything else appears as panels and dialogs.

pages.title: Operations Overview
pages.summary: Deployment, storage, security, channels, and monitoring — five main threads. The goal is to keep the system running stably over the long term.

pages.title: Deployment and Running
pages.summary: Decide on a runtime form and prepare the environment before deploying. A Hull (server) deployment needs at least a database, workspace storage, and the backend service.

pages.title: Data and Storage
pages.summary: The database, workspace, vector store, and temporary directory — what each holds, what persists, and what gets cleaned up.

pages.title: Desktop Local Mode
pages.summary: Desktop local mode is a local-first, persistent-directory-first runtime form.

pages.title: Authentication and Security
pages.summary: Tell the account types and permission levels apart, set clear security boundaries, and keep the system running within controlled limits.

pages.title: Monitoring and WunderBench
pages.summary: Observability covers distinct jobs: session monitoring watches threads, tool statistics watch hotspots, performance sampling watches the pipeline, and WunderBench watches model quality.

pages.title: WunderBench Model Evaluation
pages.summary: Use the full task bank to automatically verify how well a model completes real wunder agent tasks, and to support bank extension, regression detection, and model selection.

pages.title: Channel Runtime
pages.summary: Connecting and running external channels such as Feishu and WeChat day to day. Channel problems often lie in the access layer rather than the model.

pages.title: Reference Overview
pages.summary: The operating references and configuration notes you reach for most — where a feature lives, what a status means, and how to change a setting.

pages.title: Feature and Capability Quick Reference
pages.summary: What wunder can do and where each capability lives, organized by feature area.

pages.title: System Settings Reference
pages.summary: What the common settings mean and what to set them to.

pages.title: Session Status Guide
pages.summary: What the various statuses in a chat mean, what the agent is doing, and what to do when something goes wrong.

pages.title: Workspace Routing and File Management
pages.summary: Each user has a single cloud workspace directory. Paths are always workspace-relative, and the container parameter has been converged — directories are no longer derived per agent or container.

pages.title: Prompts and Personalization
pages.summary: Customize the agent's role and answer style — pick a built-in template, or write your own.

pages.title: Bridge Panel Guide
pages.summary: What each panel in the Bridge manages and where its entry lives.

pages.title: Architecture
pages.summary: All four forms share the same core and engine; real execution happens inside sessions, and the interface reads a bounded display view.

pages.title: Workspaces and the Working Directory
pages.summary: Each user has exactly one workspace, and tools are rooted at it: a persistent local directory in the Honeycomb, or a single per-user directory on the server in a Hull deployment.

pages.title: Sessions and Rounds
pages.summary: How a conversation is numbered: threads, user rounds, model rounds, timeline entries, and the authoritative counting conventions.

pages.title: Streaming Execution
pages.summary: Events are persisted before they are pushed, a reconnect resumes by cursor, and the frontend consumes bounded views.

pages.title: Runtime and Online Status
pages.summary: A conversation is not just static history: it also carries runtime state such as running, waiting for approval, or waiting for input, and that state tells you what the session is doing right now.

pages.title: Tool System
pages.summary: The full path a tool takes from registration and selection through dispatch to its result landing, along with parallelism, timeouts, budgets, and clipping conventions.

pages.title: Prompts and Skills
pages.summary: The system prompt shapes the agent's persona, and skills are its operating manuals for a class of task.

pages.title: Long-term Memory
pages.summary: How the agent "remembers" your preferences, background, and long-term material—structured memory is injected once when a conversation starts, then supplemented by recall as it runs.

pages.title: Quota and Token Usage
pages.summary: Each model request costs 1 credit and 1000 are granted daily; token usage is observed only and never deducted.

pages.title: Goal Mode
pages.summary: Goal mode is a session-level persistent goal driven by a model-round budget — set it once, and the agent keeps going on its own until it completes, gets blocked, or spends the budget.

pages.title: Companion System
pages.summary: A companion is a visual layer attached to an agent — a ZIP companion package plus a sprite sheet that follows the runtime state and takes no part in any execution logic.

pages.title: Boundary Handling
pages.summary: Context overflow, network interruption, tool failure, queued tasks — the system stays stable under these boundary conditions instead of crashing outright.

pages.title: Help
pages.summary: Entry page for locating a problem by symptom.

pages.title: Troubleshooting
pages.summary: Cause and check points by symptom.

pages.title: FAQ
pages.summary: Common conclusions for using wunder, ahead of symptom-level troubleshooting.

pages.title: Glossary
pages.summary: Core terms in wunder documentation, explained in plain language.

zh-CN/index.title: wunder 心舰
zh-CN/index.summary: wunder 是智能体调度平台。蜂窝是电脑上的本地 AI 工作台，蜂巢是浏览器里的云端工作台，舵机是终端入口，舰体是多人共用的管理平台。

headings.text: 四个形态，按场景选一个
一个智能体，多个任务并行

zh-CN/start/quickstart.title: 快速开始
zh-CN/start/quickstart.summary: 用最短路径把蜂窝跑起来：下载、启动、配模型、发第一条消息、验证结果。个人用户默认入口，无需部署服务。

zh-CN/start/desktop.title: 蜂窝（desktop）入门
zh-CN/start/desktop.summary: wunder 的默认使用方式：本地 AI 工作台。下载安装即可使用，不需要先部署舰体；同进程原生调用引擎，不占端口，不走 HTTP/WebSocket 中转。

headings.text: 界面结构（主窗只有两页）
蜂窝独有能力（其他界面没有）

zh-CN/start/server.title: 舰体（server）部署
zh-CN/start/server.summary: 可选形态。多人共用的用户与智能体管理平台：多租户、权限治理、渠道接入、智能体应用发布。舰体启动后同端口挂舰桥（18000），蜂巢由独立的网页服务容器下发（18001）。

zh-CN/start/cli.title: 舵机（cli）使用
zh-CN/start/cli.summary: 手工本地操作入口。终端里进交互界面，管道里自动降级为一次性执行；22 条斜杠命令、exec --json 事件流、cloud 子命令全套；舵机侧关闭定时任务与引擎排队。

headings.text: 舵机独有能力（其他界面没有）

zh-CN/start/hubs.title: 说明书总览
zh-CN/start/hubs.summary: 说明书导航页：从蜂窝起步，按需进入界面地图、其它形态与参考。start 与 surfaces 两组的全部页面都在这里。

zh-CN/start/docs-directory.title: 常用说明目录
zh-CN/start/docs-directory.summary: 仓库文档生态导航：设计文档、技术说明书、API 文档、使用说明书、性能标准与评分、功能迭代、经验教训的分工与读法。

headings.text: 其它分组（本页不列全部，只列站点主标签）
技术说明书（docs/技术说明书/）

zh-CN/concepts/index.title: 核心概览
zh-CN/concepts/index.summary: wunder 为什么这样表现——10 个核心设计约束，以及它们的分层与入口。

zh-CN/concepts/core-agent-loop.title: 智能体循环
zh-CN/concepts/core-agent-loop.summary: 你只说一次目标，剩下的步骤引擎替你跑：循环按模型轮次推进，到终态或刹车为止。

headings.text: 什么时候会自己停下来
该等、该插手、该换新线程

zh-CN/concepts/core-tools.title: 工具
zh-CN/concepts/core-tools.summary: 智能体做事的能力来自四层结构——执行体工具、可调用知识与脚本的技能、管理员选择的能力、用户自己接入的工具；四层不是一回事，「能选」不等于「能调」。

headings.text: 动态注册：模型能看到的工具不止内置清单
结果的裁剪有两条通道

zh-CN/concepts/core-context-compression.title: 上下文压缩
zh-CN/concepts/core-context-compression.summary: 长对话不会因为太长而中断：系统在必要时精简历史、保留最有效的信息，让对话继续。

zh-CN/concepts/core-memory.title: 记忆
zh-CN/concepts/core-memory.summary: 长期资料在线程创建时注入一次，之后保持冻结。它的两层结构，以及使用上的注意点。

zh-CN/concepts/core-channels.title: 渠道
zh-CN/concepts/core-channels.summary: 飞书、QQ、微信、XMPP 和通用 webhook 各自的支持范围，以及消息到智能体与工作区的绑定解析。

headings.text: 消息怎么找到智能体和工作区
入站、出站与限流的边界

zh-CN/concepts/core-scheduled-tasks.title: 定时任务
zh-CN/concepts/core-scheduled-tasks.summary: 智能体在指定时间自动执行：at 定点、every 固定间隔、cron 表达式三种排程，配租约、退避与自动禁用，进程重启不丢任务。

headings.text: 从哪里建、各形态支持情况

zh-CN/concepts/core-multi-user-managemen.title: 多用户管理
zh-CN/concepts/core-multi-user-managemen.summary: 舰体形态下的用户、单位与权限边界：登录态、在线状态、单位树、等级与额度、智能体定义文档和数据隔离。

headings.text: 登录态用的是不透明令牌
单位树与负责人作用域
等级和额度是两套东西
智能体的定义文档与线程不是一回事

zh-CN/concepts/core-realtime.title: 实时性
zh-CN/concepts/core-realtime.summary: 执行过程持续可见：WebSocket 是唯一实时通道，断线用游标补水补齐，客户端看到的始终是后端真相的投影，慢客户端会被保护性脱钩。

headings.text: 后端是真相，前端是投影
展示读取是有界分页的

zh-CN/concepts/core-stability.title: 稳定性
zh-CN/concepts/core-stability.summary: 出错不扩散、失败能恢复、问题可复盘。稳定性来自四类硬约束——有界、预算、熔断、单写者——以及出错后统一的错误结构与清楚的处置动作。

headings.text: 队列都有界，满了就报忙

zh-CN/concepts/core-observability.title: 可观测性
zh-CN/concepts/core-observability.summary: 日志、运行时指标、监控与线程轨迹、性能与压测四类入口各自的覆盖范围，以及从错误信息出发的排障顺序。

zh-CN/tools/index.title: 工具总览
zh-CN/tools/index.summary: wunder 的工具按用途分成几类；选型入口、结果形态约定，以及不套统一外壳的几个例外。

headings.text: 只有关键词，想找网页来源
要点击、输入、等页面动态渲染

zh-CN/tools/workspace-files.title: 工作区文件
zh-CN/tools/workspace-files.summary: 浏览工作区、搜索内容、读文件和写文件这几个最常用操作的使用方式。

zh-CN/tools/exec.title: 执行命令
zh-CN/tools/exec.summary: 运行 shell 命令、编译、测试或调用现成的命令行工具；支持预演、资源预算和输出守卫。

zh-CN/tools/ptc.title: ptc
zh-CN/tools/ptc.summary: ptc 是 Python 临时脚本执行工具，已从 wunder 中移除，本页仅作历史参考。

zh-CN/tools/apply-patch.title: 应用补丁
zh-CN/tools/apply-patch.summary: 用补丁文本做小范围、可审查的精确修改；`apply_patch` 已并入 `文本编辑`，不再作为独立工具暴露。

zh-CN/tools/read-image.title: 读图工具
zh-CN/tools/read-image.summary: 把本地的图片、动图或视频送进当前对话，让智能体直接看这些素材。

zh-CN/tools/skill-call.title: 技能调用
zh-CN/tools/skill-call.summary: 把一个技能的说明和目录加载进当前对话，让智能体照着技能流程干活。

zh-CN/tools/web-fetch.title: 网页抓取
zh-CN/tools/web-fetch.summary: 让智能体读取一个网页的正文，用于查资料、读文档、看接口返回。

zh-CN/tools/browser.title: 浏览器工具族
zh-CN/tools/browser.summary: 浏览器不是单个工具：启用后自动注册一组 `browser_*` 工具，用来打开页面、点击、输入、等待、截图和读取渲染后的内容。

zh-CN/tools/desktop-control.title: 桌面控制
zh-CN/tools/desktop-control.summary: 桌面控制器与桌面监视器在桌面模式下操作本机鼠标键盘、截图观察，并把画面作为视觉输入追加给模型。

zh-CN/tools/panels-and-a2ui.title: 计划面板 / 问询面板 / 会话让出
zh-CN/tools/panels-and-a2ui.summary: 三个交互控制工具：维护可见的执行计划、动手前向用户征询路线、主动让出当前轮次等待外部事件。

headings.text: 计划面板 / 问询面板 / 会话让出

zh-CN/tools/schedule-task.title: 定时任务
zh-CN/tools/schedule-task.summary: 让智能体按时间自动干活：创建、修改、查询、立即执行和启停定时任务。

headings.text: 循环任务会不会越堆越多

zh-CN/tools/final-response.title: 最终回复
zh-CN/tools/final-response.summary: 最终回复工具已从 wunder 移除，本页仅作历史参考。

zh-CN/tools/sleep.title: 会话让出
zh-CN/tools/sleep.summary: 让智能体主动结束当前轮次、把控制权交还系统，等外部结果回来再继续。

zh-CN/tools/thread-control.title: 会话线程控制
zh-CN/tools/thread-control.summary: 让智能体同时推进多件事：新建、切换、改名、归档和恢复任务线程。

zh-CN/tools/subagent-control.title: 子智能体控制
zh-CN/tools/subagent-control.summary: 让主智能体把一块独立工作派给子智能体去做，并跟踪、等待、引导和回收它们。

zh-CN/tools/memory-manager.title: 记忆管理
zh-CN/tools/memory-manager.summary: 管理当前智能体在当前用户下的长期记忆碎片：列出、搜索、读取、新增、更新、删除，以及“短索引注入 + 按需取全文”的用法。

zh-CN/tools/channel.title: 渠道工具
zh-CN/tools/channel.summary: 渠道工具已从 wunder 移除，本页仅作历史参考。

zh-CN/tools/self-status.title: 自我状态
zh-CN/tools/self-status.summary: 让智能体自查当前会话的模型、上下文占用、轮次进度和事件计数，用来判断要不要压缩上下文或收尾。

zh-CN/tools/user-world.title: 用户世界工具
zh-CN/tools/user-world.summary: 查询站内有哪些用户，并给站内用户发消息。

zh-CN/tools/a2a-tools.title: A2A 工具
zh-CN/tools/a2a-tools.summary: A2A 工具已从 wunder 移除，本页仅作历史参考。

zh-CN/integration/index.title: 接入概览
zh-CN/integration/index.summary: 把 wunder 接进现有系统前，先选对接口域：单次执行、聊天会话、工作区、临时转换、外部渠道、免登嵌入、A2A 与 MCP，各有各的入口。

zh-CN/integration/wunder-api.title: wunder API
zh-CN/integration/wunder-api.summary: 把 wunder 当成一个执行能力来调用，一次请求出一次结果；要做完整聊天产品再转到会话域。

headings.text: 最短链路：稳定绑定智能体

zh-CN/integration/chat-ws.title: 聊天 WebSocket
zh-CN/integration/chat-ws.summary: 聊天的实时通道，同时也是会话控制通道：启动执行、断线续传、观察、取消、回传审批都在同一条连接上。

zh-CN/integration/chat-sessions.title: 聊天会话
zh-CN/integration/chat-sessions.summary: 做聊天产品时用的会话接口：创建会话、收发消息、附件预处理、恢复与取消，都在这个域里。

headings.text: 最短链路：接通一个会话

zh-CN/integration/workspace-api.title: 工作区 API
zh-CN/integration/workspace-api.summary: 工作区不只管文件读写，它把每个用户固定到属于自己的唯一云端目录。

zh-CN/integration/temp-dir.title: 临时目录与文档转换
zh-CN/integration/temp-dir.summary: 临时上传、下载和中转都走临时目录；文档、音频、视频在进入会话前先做一次转换或媒体处理。

headings.text: 临时目录与工作区的分工
为什么拿到的是下载链接

zh-CN/integration/user-world.title: 用户世界接口
zh-CN/integration/user-world.summary: 用户和用户之间的单聊、群聊、已读状态都在这里，和用户对智能体的会话是两套并行的域。

headings.text: 最短链路：接一个完整客户端

zh-CN/integration/channel-webhook.title: 渠道 Webhook
zh-CN/integration/channel-webhook.summary: 外部渠道发来的消息（飞书、微信、QQ、XMPP 等）统一从一个 Webhook 地址进来，再交给后台异步处理。

zh-CN/integration/weixin-channel.title: 微信 iLink 渠道
zh-CN/integration/weixin-channel.summary: 新微信渠道用 iLink 协议，跟旧的公众号、企业微信不是一套。

zh-CN/integration/external-login.title: 外部登录与免登嵌入
zh-CN/integration/external-login.summary: 把外部系统里已登录的用户直接带进 wunder，免去再输一次密码；既能跳聊天页，也能跳到指定智能体。

headings.text: 最短链路：外部身份换 wunder 会话

zh-CN/integration/a2a.title: A2A 接口
zh-CN/integration/a2a.summary: wunder 既能把能力按 A2A 协议暴露给别的智能体系统，也能把外部 A2A 服务挂成工具供模型调用。

headings.text: 最短链路：让外部调 wunder
最短链路：让 wunder 调外部

en/index.title: wunder
en/index.summary: wunder is an agent orchestration platform. The Honeycomb is the local AI workbench on your computer, the Beehive is the cloud workbench in a browser, the Helm is the terminal entry point, and the Hull is the shared management platform for teams.
read_when: You are new to wunder and choosing which form to use
You want the entry point to the whole manual

en/start/quickstart.title: Quick Start
en/start/quickstart.summary: The shortest path to get the Honeycomb running: download, launch, configure a model, send your first message, verify the result. The default entry point for individual users, with no service to deploy.
read_when: You are an individual user setting up wunder for the first time
You want the fastest path from install to a completed first task

headings.text: What a working setup looks like
Where to look when something breaks

en/start/desktop.title: Starting with the Honeycomb (Desktop)
en/start/desktop.summary: wunder's default way to work: a local AI workbench. Download, install, open, go — no Hull to deploy first; it calls the engine natively in-process, takes no port, and routes through no HTTP/WebSocket relay.

en/start/server.title: Deploying the Hull (Server)
en/start/server.summary: An optional form. The user-and-agent management platform for multi-user sharing: multi-tenancy, permission governance, channel integration, and agent-app publishing. Once the Hull is up, the Bridge (18000) is served on the same port, and the Beehive is delivered by a separate web-service container (18001).

You need its ports, config precedence, or first-login checklist

headings.text: The three pieces and their ports

en/start/cli.title: Using the Helm (CLI)
en/start/cli.summary: The manual local entry point. In a terminal it opens an interactive session; in a pipeline it degrades to a one-shot run. The full set of 22 slash commands, an exec --json event stream, and the complete cloud subcommand family; scheduled tasks and engine queueing are off on the Helm.

You need the cloud subcommands to operate device interlink from a shell

headings.text: What only the Helm can do

en/start/docs-directory.summary: A guide to the repo's documentation ecosystem: how the overview and design docs, technical manual, API reference, user manual, performance standards and scoring, changelog, and lessons-learned divide the work, and how to read them.

en/concepts/index.title: Core Concepts
en/concepts/index.summary: Why wunder behaves the way it does—10 core design constraints, along with the layers they form, the entries into them, and the reading paths.

en/concepts/core-agent-loop.title: Agent Loop
en/concepts/core-agent-loop.summary: You state the goal once and the engine runs the remaining steps; the loop advances round by round until it reaches a deliverable result or hits a brake.

headings.text: When it stops on its own
The thread is the unit of execution
When to wait, when to step in, when to open a new thread

en/concepts/core-tools.title: Tools
en/concepts/core-tools.summary: The agent's ability to act comes from a four-layer structure: executor tools, skills that package callable knowledge and scripts, capabilities the administrator selects, and tools the user connects. Keeping the layers distinct is what keeps "selectable" separate from "invokable".

headings.text: Dynamic registration: the model sees more than the built-in list
Result trimming runs on two tracks

en/concepts/core-context-compression.title: Context Compression
en/concepts/core-context-compression.summary: Long conversations are not cut short when they grow long. The system trims history in graded levels, keeps the most useful information, and lets the conversation continue.

headings.text: What it protects and what it leaves alone

en/concepts/core-memory.title: Memory
en/concepts/core-memory.summary: Long-term data is injected once when a thread is created and stays frozen afterwards; it has two layers, initialization injection and runtime recall.

headings.text: A few rules that go with it

en/concepts/core-channels.title: Channels
en/concepts/core-channels.summary: Feishu, QQ, WeChat, XMPP, and generic webhooks differ in support level; an inbound message is routed to its agent and workspace by binding.

headings.text: A channel is only an entry point
How a message finds its agent and workspace
The boundaries of inbound, outbound, and rate limiting

en/concepts/core-scheduled-tasks.title: Scheduled Tasks
en/concepts/core-scheduled-tasks.summary: Scheduled tasks run the agent at a chosen time: three schedule kinds — at for a one-off point, every for a fixed interval, cron for a recurring pattern — with leases, backoff, and auto-disable, so tasks survive a process restart.
read_when: You want a report, inspection, or reminder to run on a schedule instead of by hand
A scheduled task did not run, ran twice, or was disabled on its own
You need to know which forms support scheduling and which do not

headings.text: Where to create one, and support by form

en/concepts/core-multi-user-management.title: Multi-user Management
en/concepts/core-multi-user-management.summary: User, unit, and permission boundaries in the Hull form: login state, presence, the unit tree, levels and quotas, agent definition documents, and data isolation.

headings.text: The unit tree and the unit-head scope
Levels and quotas are two different things
An agent's definition document is not the same thing as a thread

en/concepts/core-realtime.title: Realtime
en/concepts/core-realtime.summary: The realtime channel runs on WebSocket; a reconnect catches up by cursor; what the client sees is a projection of backend truth; slow clients are uncoupled to protect the stream.

headings.text: The backend is truth, the frontend is a projection
Chat streaming runs only over WebSocket
Display reads are bounded and paged

en/concepts/core-stability.title: Stability
en/concepts/core-stability.summary: Errors that do not spread, failures that can recover, and problems that can be reviewed. Stability comes from four kinds of hard constraint — bounds, budgets, circuit breaking, and a single writer — plus a consistent error structure and clear actions when something goes wrong.

headings.text: Every queue is bounded, and a full queue reports busy
Session locks and the single writer
What an error looks like from the outside
Whether to wait or to act

en/concepts/core-observability.title: Observability
en/concepts/core-observability.summary: Logs, runtime metrics and alerts, monitoring and thread traces, and performance testing each cover their own area; failures are worked through in a fixed order from the error message onward.

en/tools/index.summary: wunder's tools are grouped by purpose: selection entry points by situation, the conventions for how results are shaped, and a few exceptions.

en/tools/workspace-files.summary: Browsing the workspace, searching content, reading files, and writing files.

en/tools/exec.summary: Run shell commands, compile, test, or call an existing command-line tool; it supports previews, resource budgets, and output guards.

en/tools/ptc.summary: ptc was the temporary Python script execution tool; it has been removed from wunder, and this page is a historical reference.

en/tools/apply-patch.title: Apply Patch
en/tools/apply-patch.summary: Use patch text for small, reviewable, precise edits; `apply_patch` has been merged into `Text Edit`.

en/tools/read-image.title: Read Image
en/tools/read-image.summary: Send a local image, animated GIF, or video into the current conversation so the agent can look at the material directly.

en/tools/skill-call.title: Skill Call
en/tools/skill-call.summary: Loading a skill's instructions and its directory into the current conversation so the agent can work through that skill's process.

en/tools/web-fetch.title: Web Fetch
en/tools/web-fetch.summary: Letting the agent read the body of a web page, for looking things up, reading docs, or inspecting API responses.

en/tools/browser.title: Browser Tools
en/tools/browser.summary: The browser is not a single tool: once enabled it registers a group of `browser_*` tools for opening pages, clicking, typing, waiting, taking screenshots, and reading rendered content.

en/tools/desktop-control.title: Desktop Control
en/tools/desktop-control.summary: In desktop mode, the Desktop Controller and Desktop Monitor drive the local mouse and keyboard, capture screenshots, and feed the picture to the model as appended visual input.

en/tools/panels-and-a2ui.title: Plan Panel / Question Panel / Sessions Yield
en/tools/panels-and-a2ui.summary: Three interaction-control tools: maintaining a visible execution plan, asking the user for a route before acting, and yielding the current turn to wait for an external event.

en/tools/schedule-task.title: Schedule Task
en/tools/schedule-task.summary: Creates, changes, inspects, runs right away, and enables or disables scheduled jobs.

headings.text: Recurring jobs do not pile up

en/tools/final-response.title: Final Response
en/tools/final-response.summary: The Final Response tool has been removed from wunder; kept only as a historical reference.

en/tools/sleep.title: Sessions Yield
en/tools/sleep.summary: Letting the agent stop the current turn on purpose, hand control back to the system, and carry on once an external result arrives.

headings.text: How it differs from a final reply
Do not use it to wait for commands

en/tools/thread-control.title: Thread Control
en/tools/thread-control.summary: Letting the agent move several things forward at once: create, switch, rename, archive, and restore task threads.

en/tools/subagent-control.title: Subagent Control
en/tools/subagent-control.summary: Letting the main agent hand a self-contained piece of work to subagents, then track, wait on, guide, and reclaim them.

en/tools/memory-manager.title: Memory Manager
en/tools/memory-manager.summary: Manage the current agent's long-term memory fragments under the current user: list, search, read, add, update, and remove, along with the "short index injection plus fetch-on-demand" pattern.

en/tools/channel.title: Channel Tool
en/tools/channel.summary: The channel tool has been removed from wunder; kept only as a historical reference.

en/tools/self-status.title: Self Status
en/tools/self-status.summary: Checks the current session's model, context usage, round progress, and event counts, for deciding whether to compress context or wrap up.

en/tools/user-world.title: User World
en/tools/user-world.summary: Looking up which users exist inside the site, and sending messages to users inside the site.

en/tools/a2a-tools.title: A2A Tools
en/tools/a2a-tools.summary: A2A tools have been removed from wunder; kept only as a historical reference.

en/integration/chat-ws.title: Chat WebSocket

en/integration/workspace-api.title: Workspace API
en/integration/workspace-api.summary: The workspace does more than file read and write — it pins every user to their own single cloud directory.

en/integration/temp-dir.title: Temp Directory and Document Conversion
en/integration/temp-dir.summary: Temporary uploads, downloads, and transit all go through the temp directory; documents, audio, and video get one conversion or media pass before they enter a session.

headings.text: Why What You Get Back Is a Download Link

en/integration/user-world.title: User World API
en/integration/user-world.summary: One-to-one chats, group chats, and read state between users all live here, parallel to the user-to-agent conversation domain.

en/integration/channel-webhook.title: Channel Webhook
en/integration/channel-webhook.summary: Inbound messages from external channels (Feishu, WeChat, QQ, XMPP, and others) all arrive through a single Webhook address and are then handled asynchronously in the background.

en/integration/weixin-channel.title: WeChat iLink Channel
en/integration/weixin-channel.summary: The new WeChat channel uses the iLink protocol and is not the same thing as the legacy Official Account or WeCom channels.

en/integration/external-login.title: External Login and Embedding
en/integration/external-login.summary: Bring users who are already logged in to an external system straight into wunder without asking them to type a password again; they can land on the chat page or on a specific agent.

headings.text: Exchanging an External Identity for a wunder Session

en/integration/a2a.title: A2A Interface
en/integration/a2a.summary: wunder both exposes its capabilities to other agent systems over the A2A protocol and mounts external A2A services as tools the model can call.

en/integration/mcp-endpoint.title: MCP Endpoint
en/integration/mcp-endpoint.summary: wunder can both expose itself as an MCP service and act as an MCP client to connect to external services.
